title: Hypotheticals, regrets and the irrealis
objectives: Use kung sakali and sakaling for remote or precautionary conditions
Express counterfactuals with kung hindi (lang) dahil sa and kung + completed aspect
Voice regrets and missed obligations with sana + completed aspect and dapat sana
Distinguish real conditions (kapag), open conditions (kung), and unreal conditions in extended speech

grammar.title: kung sakali and sakaling: the 'just in case' zone
grammar.explanation:
You know kung for open conditions and kapag for habitual/expected ones. B2 adds the remote condition: kung sakali (man) 'if by any chance, in the event that' and its clipped form sakaling + clause. These flag the condition as unlikely or merely precautionary: Kung sakaling umulan, nasa kotse ang payong — 'In case it rains, the umbrella is in the car.' Dalhin mo ang resume mo, kung sakali — 'Bring your resume, just in case' (kung sakali can dangle at the end exactly like English 'just in case').

Sakaling attaches directly to a verb, usually contemplated aspect: Sakaling matuloy ang biyahe, tatawagan kita. Adding man (kung sakali man) makes it even more remote and concessive: Kung sakali mang hindi ako makarating, magsimula na kayo — 'If ever I can't make it, go ahead and start.'

Don't overuse it: for plain likely conditions, stick to kung/kapag. Kung sakali colors the whole sentence with 'this probably won't happen, but let's cover it'.

grammar.title: Counterfactuals: kung + completed, and kung hindi (lang) dahil sa
grammar.explanation:
Tagalog builds 'if X had happened' with plain kung plus the completed aspect, letting context signal unreality: Kung nag-aral ako nang mabuti, nakapasa sana ako — 'If I had studied hard, I would have passed.' The sana in the main clause is what marks the outcome as unreal; without it the sentence can read as a real past possibility.

To say an outcome was prevented by one decisive factor, use kung hindi dahil sa 'if not for': Kung hindi dahil sa iyo, nalunod na ako — 'If not for you, I would have drowned.' Adding lang sharpens the 'only thing in the way' feel: Kung hindi lang umulan, natuloy sana ang parada — 'If only it hadn't rained, the parade would have pushed through.' Kung hindi lang + clause is also how you grumble about the single obstacle: Kung hindi lang ako pagod, sasama ako.

Pattern to internalize: unreal condition = kung + (hindi lang) + completed/adjective; unreal result = verb + sana (often completed or contemplated). Sana can attach to either clause, but the result clause is its most common home.

grammar.title: Regret and hindsight: sana + completed, dapat sana, muntik na
grammar.explanation:
Sana with a contemplated verb is a hope (Sana pumasa ako — 'I hope I pass'). Shift the verb to completed aspect and the hope curdles into regret about the past: Sana pumasa ako would become Sana nakapasa ako 'I wish I had passed'; Sana sinabi mo agad 'You should have told me right away / I wish you had said so immediately.'

Dapat sana + verb is hindsight obligation, English 'should have': Dapat sana ay nagpaalam ka muna — 'You should have asked permission first.' Dapat sana akong sumama — 'I should have come along.' The word order is flexible: dapat sana can precede the whole clause or hug the verb. Note the contrast: dapat + verb alone is a present/future obligation ('should'), dapat sana pushes it into the unreal past ('should have, but didn't').

Round out the irrealis toolkit with muntik na 'almost (but didn't happen)': Muntik na akong mahulog — 'I almost fell.' Muntik na takes the same -ng linker and a contemplated or root-like verb form. Together: Muntik na kaming ma-late; dapat sana ay umalis tayo nang mas maaga — 'We were almost late; we should have left earlier.'

vocab.en: if by any chance, in case
vocab.note: can stand alone at the end of a sentence: '..., kung sakali.'

example.tl: Magdala ka ng jacket, kung sakali.
example.en: Bring a jacket, just in case.

vocab.en: in the event that, should (it happen that)
vocab.note: clipped form of kung sakaling; attaches straight to the verb

example.tl: Sakaling ma-traffic, mag-text ka lang.
example.en: Should you get stuck in traffic, just text.

vocab.en: if not for, were it not for

example.tl: Kung hindi dahil sa scholarship, hindi ako nakatapos.
example.en: If not for the scholarship, I would not have graduated.

vocab.en: if only ... not; if it weren't for

example.tl: Kung hindi lang malayo, araw-araw akong dadalaw.
example.en: If only it weren't far, I would visit every day.

example.tl: Dapat sana ay tumawag ka bago ka pumunta.
example.en: You should have called before coming over.

example.tl: Muntik na kaming maiwan ng barko.
example.en: We were almost left behind by the ship.

vocab.en: to regret (a loss or missed chance)

example.tl: Pinanghinayangan niya ang trabahong tinanggihan niya.
example.en: She regretted the job she had turned down.

vocab.en: what a waste; what a pity
vocab.note: also a verb root: masayang 'to be wasted'

example.tl: Sayang! Isang punto na lang, panalo na tayo.
example.en: What a pity! One more point and we would have won.

example.tl: Huwag mong palampasin ang ganitong pagkakataon.
example.en: Don't let an opportunity like this pass.

vocab.en: to let (something) pass, to miss (a chance)

example.tl: Pinalampas ko ang huling biyahe kagabi.
example.en: I let the last trip pass last night.

example.tl: Baka magsisi ka kung hindi ka susubok.
example.en: You might regret it if you don't try.

example.tl: Naiwan ko na naman ang pitaka ko sa bahay.
example.en: I left my wallet at home again.

example.tl: Hindi natuloy ang piknik dahil sa bagyo.
example.en: The picnic didn't push through because of the storm.

example.tl: Nakaligtaan kong i-save ang file bago ko isinara.
example.en: I forgot to save the file before I closed it.

example.tl: Paghandaan natin ang anumang posibleng mangyari.
example.en: Let's prepare for anything that could happen.

example.tl: May posibilidad na ilipat ang eksamen sa Lunes.
example.en: There's a possibility the exam will be moved to Monday.

example.tl: Alam niya ang panganib, pero sumugod pa rin siya.
example.en: He knew the danger, but he pressed on anyway.

example.tl: Naligtas ang lahat ng pasahero ng lumubog na bangka.
example.en: All the passengers of the sunken boat were saved.

example.tl: Muntik na siyang malunod sa ilog noong bata siya.
example.en: He almost drowned in the river when he was a child.

vocab.en: to ask permission; to say goodbye

example.tl: Nagpaalam muna siya sa mga magulang bago umalis.
example.en: She asked her parents' permission before leaving.

example.tl: Tinanggihan niya ang alok na trabaho sa Singapore.
example.en: He turned down the job offer in Singapore.

example.tl: Mabuti ang alok nila, pero kailangan ko pang mag-isip.
example.en: Their offer is good, but I still need to think.

example.tl: Tawagan mo ako sakaling magbago ang isip mo.
example.en: Call me should you change your mind.

vocab.en: to chase after; to try to catch up

example.tl: Humabol siya sa bus pero hindi na inabutan.
example.en: He ran after the bus but didn't catch it.

example.tl: Kung maagap ka lang, nakuha mo sana ang diskwento.
example.en: If you had just acted promptly, you would have gotten the discount.

example.tl: Tutuparin ko ang pangako ko, kahit anong mangyari.
example.en: I will keep my promise, no matter what happens.

dialogue.title: Ang alok na hindi na maibabalik
dialogue.context: Over coffee, Dennis tells his friend Grace about a job offer abroad that he turned down years ago.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.tl: Totoo bang inalok ka dati ng trabaho sa Canada? Bakit hindi ka umalis?
lines.en: Is it true you were once offered a job in Canada? Why didn't you leave?

lines.speaker: Dennis
lines.tl: Totoo. Tinanggihan ko, kasi bago pa lang kaming kasal noon ni Marie.
lines.en: It's true. I turned it down, because Marie and I were newly married then.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.en: And now, do you regret it?

lines.speaker: Dennis
lines.tl: Minsan. Kung tinanggap ko sana, malamang may sarili na kaming bahay ngayon.
lines.en: Sometimes. If I had accepted, we would probably have our own house by now.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.tl: Pero kung umalis ka noon, hindi mo sana nasaksihan ang paglaki ng mga anak mo.
lines.en: But if you had left back then, you wouldn't have witnessed your children growing up.

lines.speaker: Dennis
lines.tl: Tama ka. Kung hindi lang talaga mahirap ang buhay dito, wala akong ni katiting na pagsisisi.
lines.en: You're right. If only life weren't so hard here, I wouldn't have even a shred of regret.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.tl: Alam mo, dapat sana ay pinag-usapan ninyo nang mas matagal noon. Mukhang mabilis ang desisyon mo.
lines.en: You know, you two should have discussed it longer back then. It sounds like your decision was quick.

lines.speaker: Dennis
lines.tl: Oo, isang gabi lang. Muntik na nga akong magbago ng isip sa airport ng pinsan ko, habang naghahatid kami.
lines.en: Yes, just one night. I actually almost changed my mind at my cousin's airport send-off, while we were seeing him off.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.tl: E kung sakaling mag-alok ulit sila ngayon? Tatanggapin mo ba?
lines.en: And if by any chance they offered again now? Would you accept?

lines.speaker: Dennis
lines.tl: Sakaling mangyari 'yon, sasabihin ko muna kina Marie at sa mga bata. Hindi na ako magdedesisyon nang mag-isa.
lines.en: Should that happen, I'd talk to Marie and the kids first. I won't decide alone anymore.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.tl: 'Yan ang tamang aral mula sa lahat ng ito.
lines.en: That's the right lesson from all of this.

reading.title: Ang bagyong hindi namin pinaghandaan
reading.tl:
Hanggang ngayon, tuwing malakas ang ulan, naaalala ko ang gabing iyon noong 2013. Nasa ikatlong taon ako sa hayskul, at kababalita pa lang sa radyo na may paparating na bagyo. "Karaniwang bagyo lang iyan," sabi ng mga matatanda sa amin. Hindi kami naghanda. Hindi namin binili ang mga kandila, hindi namin itinaas ang mga gamit, at hindi kami lumikas.

Nang hatinggabi, mabilis na tumaas ang tubig. Muntik nang maiwan ang lola ko sa kuwarto niya sa ibaba; kung hindi lang siya sinigawan ng tatay ko, hindi na sana siya nakaakyat. Umakyat kaming lahat sa bubong at doon naghintay ng umaga, basang-basa at nanginginig.

Naligtas kaming lahat, salamat sa Diyos. Pero maraming kapitbahay ang nawalan ng bahay, at may mga hindi na nakabalik pa. Dapat sana ay nakinig kami sa babala. Dapat sana ay lumikas kami nang maaga. Kung naghanda lang kami, hindi sana namin naranasan ang takot na iyon.

Ngayon, ako na ang nagtuturo sa aming barangay tungkol sa paghahanda sa sakuna. Laging may nakahandang bag sa tabi ng pinto namin: flashlight, tubig, de-lata, mga dokumento. Sinasabi ko sa mga kabataan: huwag ninyong hintaying maranasan ang aming naranasan. Sakaling dumating muli ang ganoong bagyo, handa na dapat tayo. Ang panghihinayang ay laging huli; ang paghahanda ay laging nasa oras.
reading.en:
Until now, whenever the rain is heavy, I remember that night in 2013. I was in my third year of high school, and the radio had only just reported that a storm was approaching. "That's just an ordinary storm," the elders around us said. We did not prepare. We didn't buy candles, we didn't raise our belongings, and we didn't evacuate.

At midnight, the water rose fast. My grandmother was almost trapped in her room downstairs; if my father hadn't shouted for her, she would not have made it upstairs. We all climbed onto the roof and waited there for morning, soaked and shivering.

We were all saved, thank God. But many neighbors lost their homes, and some never came back. We should have listened to the warning. We should have evacuated early. If we had only prepared, we would not have experienced that fear.

Now I am the one who teaches our barangay about disaster preparedness. There is always a packed bag beside our door: flashlight, water, canned goods, documents. I tell the young people: don't wait to experience what we experienced. Should such a storm come again, we must already be ready. Regret always comes late; preparation is always on time.

gloss.en: regret (over a loss or missed chance)

exercises.prompt: Which sentence best expresses 'Bring cash, just in case'?
choices: Magdala ka ng cash, kung sakali.
Magdala ka ng cash, kapag lagi.
Magdala ka ng cash, dahil sakali.
Magdala ka ng cash, sana lang.
exercises.explain: Kung sakali can dangle at the end of a sentence exactly like English 'just in case'. The other options are ungrammatical combinations.

exercises.prompt: Sana sinabi mo sa akin kahapon. What is the speaker doing?
choices: Hoping you will tell them tomorrow
Expressing regret that you didn't tell them yesterday
Reporting what you said yesterday
Asking permission to speak
exercises.explain: Sana + completed aspect (sinabi) is a regret about the past: 'I wish you had told me yesterday.' With a contemplated verb it would be a hope about the future.

exercises.prompt: ___ sana ay nagpaalam ka muna bago mo hiniram ang kotse. (should have)
exercises.explain: Dapat sana + verb = 'should have (but didn't)'. Plain dapat without sana would be a present obligation.

exercises.prompt: Muntik na akong madapa sa hagdan. What happened?
choices: I fell down the stairs.
I almost tripped on the stairs but didn't.
I often trip on the stairs.
I will probably trip on the stairs.
exercises.explain: Muntik na marks a near-event that did not actually occur: 'I almost tripped.' If the fall had happened, you'd just say nadapa ako.

exercises.prompt: Tawagan mo ako ___ magbago ang isip mo. (should it happen that)
exercises.hint: the clipped conditional that attaches straight to the clause
exercises.explain: Sakaling (or kung sakaling) introduces a remote condition: 'should you change your mind'. Plain kung would also be grammatical but loses the 'unlikely but possible' color the sentence asks for.

exercises.tl: Kung hindi lang bumagyo, natuloy sana ang kasal nila sa beach.
choices: If only there hadn't been a storm, their beach wedding would have pushed through.
Because of the storm, they moved the wedding to the beach.
Their beach wedding pushed through despite the storm.
They hope there will be no storm at their beach wedding.
exercises.explain: Kung hindi lang + completed (bumagyo) names the single obstacle; natuloy sana marks the unrealized outcome: the wedding did not push through.

exercises.prompt: If not for my neighbor, my dog would not have been saved.
exercises.answer: Kung hindi dahil sa kapitbahay ko, hindi sana naligtas ang aso ko.
accept: Kung hindi dahil sa kapitbahay ko, hindi sana naligtas ang aso ko
Kung hindi dahil sa aking kapitbahay, hindi sana naligtas ang aking aso
Hindi sana naligtas ang aso ko kung hindi dahil sa kapitbahay ko
exercises.explain: Kung hindi dahil sa X = 'if not for X'; the unreal outcome takes sana with the completed naligtas.

exercises.prompt: Pinanghinayangan niya ang pagkakataong pinalampas niya noong bata pa siya.
exercises.answer: He regretted the opportunity he let pass when he was still young.
accept: He regretted the opportunity he let pass when he was still young
She regretted the chance she let pass when she was young
He regretted the chance that he passed up when he was still young
exercises.explain: Panghinayangan is 'to regret (a loss)'; pagkakataong pinalampas niya is a relative clause, 'the opportunity that he let pass'.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct connector: '___ dumating ang bagyo, nakahanda na dapat ang inyong mga gamit.' (Should the storm arrive...)
choices: Sakaling
Sayang
Muntik nang
Dapat sanang
exercises.explain: Sakaling introduces the remote future condition 'should the storm arrive'. Sayang is 'what a waste', muntik na is 'almost', dapat sana is 'should have'.

exercises.prompt: We should have evacuated early; we almost didn't make it.
exercises.answer: Dapat sana ay lumikas kami nang maaga; muntik na kaming hindi umabot.
accept: Dapat sana ay lumikas kami nang maaga; muntik na kaming hindi umabot
Dapat sana kaming lumikas nang maaga; muntik na kaming hindi umabot
Dapat sana lumikas kami nang maaga, muntik na kaming hindi umabot
exercises.explain: Dapat sana + verb gives the hindsight obligation; muntik na + linked clause gives the near-miss. Lumikas 'to evacuate' comes from the unit's disaster vocabulary.

exercises.tl: Sayang! Kung nag-aral lang ako nang mas mabuti, nakapasa sana ako sa board exam.
choices: Regret: had they studied harder, they would have passed the board exam.
Relief: they passed the board exam after studying hard.
A plan to study harder for the next board exam.
Doubt about whether the board exam results are correct.
exercises.explain: Sayang signals regret; kung + completed (nag-aral) plus nakapasa sana forms the counterfactual: the passing never happened.

exercises.prompt: Read: 'Hindi kami naghanda. Dapat sana ay nakinig kami sa babala. Sakaling dumating muli ang ganoong bagyo, handa na dapat tayo.' Which statement is true?
choices: The family prepared well and survived easily.
The speaker regrets not heeding the warning and urges readiness for a future storm.
The speaker doubts another storm will ever come.
The warning arrived after the storm had passed.
exercises.explain: Dapat sana ay nakinig kami = regret ('we should have listened'); sakaling dumating muli sets up the precaution for a possible future storm — regret about the past, readiness for the future.
